attrs.evidence: GPT-5.6's reframing, and it is a better question than 'how many artifacts are there'. Its first cut names seven candidate canonical registries (claims/invariants; contracts + authority policy; objectives + evaluators; operations/stations; evidence + instruments; artifacts/lineage; root-of-trust/reflection) and pushes the periodic table rendering, the implication basis, the occupancy map, the conservation matrix, Pareto/QD views, metrology dashboards and independence reports to derived. The removal test it proposes is the right one: drop an artifact as authoritative, permit the rest plus derivation, and ask whether every historical incident can still be expressed AND mechanically refused. NOBODY HAS RUN IT. Fable's MOS-NINE-AUDIT claimed all nine artifacts pass the admission rule and was proposed at MEASURED; that is an admission audit, not a minimality result, and it should not carry a MEASURED status until the removal test executes.
attrs.gap: R5 builds three registries and one derived view without ruling on the seven-registry hypothesis. That is deliberate: the three built are the ones whose absence was costing something, and the count is not yet a claim.
attrs.statement: Which Mosaic artifacts are authoritative sources of truth and which are reproducibly derived views?
